Are you talking about illegal drugs or medical drugs?

The ratio of the molecule in question compared to whatever's added might be one of the key factors. Illegal drugs are usually cut to produce more $€£, medical (generic) drugs have added chemicals and manufacturing process differs from one manufacturer to the other.

I'd say that it depends on all the middlemen. The product that you would buy from a dealer on the street is 'cut' with anything from baby powder to rat poison, depending on what you're buying and who from. Basically they'll start with x kilos of a product and mix something with it to make it x times 2 kilos. Generally it'll be cut with something harmless if you're getting party drugs like ecstasy and what not but if you're looking for the latest meth/heroin gutter hybrid ugly shit then who knows what is really in that product. I guess that's how sometimes certain batches will seem stronger then others.

Sometimes it can be other things too, like how it has been stored and if it has been stored correctly and with something like acid, that you would normally get in 'stamps', it would depend on how much of a dose has been dropped on that stamp in the first place. Generally it starts it's life in liquid form and measured out from there.

Just because they are the same molecules, doesn't mean that the production process is the same. In legal drug manufacturing, the process is pretty much the same. But for illegal drug manufacturers, it may not be exactly the same. So Drug Dealer A may have an extra something to "enhance things" whilst Drug Dealer B may not.
